Subject: OpsFlow integration: SDK onramp & next steps

Hi Daniel —

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and a proposed onramp so your engineers can validate end-to-end with minimal friction. Attaching a short playbook and a bundle of sample apps.

Top takeaways (from our notes):
- Primary use case: searchable KB + assistant + structured tool-calling for ticket triage
- Preferred model family: open LLMs for cost control; fallback to higher-tier models for low-latency SLA routes
- Data flow: embeddings for retrieval, reranker for top-N, tool calls for ticket actions
- Security ask: verify SSO + data residency requirements (you flagged EU data for a subset)

Proposed immediate onramp (3 steps):
1) Local SDK quickstart (Python + TypeScript) — run sample apps against Redwood hosted sandbox credentials to validate auth, routing, and structured output.
2) Smoke tests — embeddings indexing on a small dataset, run reranker presets and test tool-calling dry-run.
3) Live lab — 30–60m pairing with Ben to exercise batching/kv-cache and observe latency.

Quick logistics/questions for you:
- Can you confirm whether the test dataset will include EU-only records (we need to scope routing)?
- Do you prefer SAML SSO or API key for the initial sandbox? We can enable short-lived API keys for dev testing.
- Any firewall/proxy constraints for outbound HTTPS to our sandbox?

Attachments:
- redwood-opsflow-sdk-playbook-v1.pdf (6 pages) — step-by-step SDK commands, env var list, and smoke test checklist
- redwood-sdk-sample-apps.tar.gz — two sample apps: ts-slack-assistant, py-search-reranker

If that plan looks good I can open a HubSpot task and schedule a live lab with Ben next week.

Thanks,

Ava Chen
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Thanks, Ava — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications before we spin up the team:

1) Data residency: we have a subset of customer records that must remain in EU. Will the sandbox let us simulate routing to EU-only model endpoints?
2) On-prem option: our security folks asked whether Redwood supports an on-prem/private deployment for the production rollout (we're in early procurement).
3) SSO: we prefer SAML in prod; for dev we can use short-lived API keys.

Also, can your sample apps show how embeddings + reranker work together (small dataset of ~5k docs)?

—Daniel

On Sat, Apr 10, 2027 at 10:17 AM Daniel Park <daniel.park@opsflow.com> wrote:
> Thanks, Ava — this looks promising. A couple quick clarifications before we spin up the team:
>
> 1) Data residency: we have a subset of customer records that must remain in EU. Will the sandbox let us simulate routing to EU-only model endpoints?
> 2) On-prem option: our security folks asked whether Redwood supports an on-prem/private deployment for the production rollout (we're in early procurement).
> 3) SSO: we prefer SAML in prod; for dev we can use short-lived API keys.
>
> Also, can your sample apps show how embeddings + reranker work together (small dataset of ~5k docs)?

Great questions — answers below plus quick local commands to get your devs started.

Answers:
- Sandbox routing: yes — sandbox supports regional routing rules. You can set REDWOOD_REGION=eu to force EU endpoints and a routing policy in the sample config (we include the mapping in the playbook).
- On-prem/private: Redwood Private is available; I'll have our sales engineer follow up on packaging + license terms. For on-prem testing we can provide an air-gapped bundle, but the usual path is: validate on hosted sandbox -> Dedicated -> Private.
- SSO: SAML in prod is fully supported. For dev, we recommend short-lived API keys or OAuth/OIDC with a dev client.
- Embeddings + reranker: the py-search-reranker app in the samples does exactly that — index -> embed -> retrieve -> rerank -> return structured hits. It runs on ~5k docs locally; the playbook includes perf knobs.

Local quickstart (condensed):

Python (virtualenv)
1) git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sample-apps.git
2) cd sample-apps/py-search-reranker
3) python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
4) pip install -r requirements.txt
5) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_...   # use the sandbox API key in the attached playbook
6) export REDWOOD_REGION=us   # or eu to validate regional routing
7) python scripts/build_index.py --dataset sample_docs.json --embed-model open-embed-v1
8) python app.py --port 8080   # hits the local microserver and demonstrates rerank flow

TypeScript (Node)
1) cd sample-apps/ts-slack-assistant
2) npm install
3) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_test_...
4) export REDWOOD_REGION=us
5) npm run dev  # local Slack slash-commands + tool-calling simulator

Smoke tests (included in playbook):
- index 100 docs, run 50 retrievals measuring p50/p95 latency
- validate structured-output JSON schema for tool calls
- run reranker with top-20 candidates and confirm improved MRR on our small eval set

Attachments again: redwood-opsflow-sdk-playbook-v1.pdf (contains the full env var list, Docker Compose for local sandbox proxy if you have firewall constraints, and the smoke-test checklist).

Next steps I propose:
- You confirm EU-data subset and preferred dev auth (SAML/OAuth/API key)
- We schedule a 45-minute lab with Ben this week to run the smoke tests and tweak batching settings

If you like, I can also push a HubSpot task that includes the playbook and links to a pre-provisioned sandbox API key.

Thanks — happy to run the lab.

Ava

Nice plan — quick technical note for the lab: start with batch_size=8 and kv_cache_enabled=true for the reranker flow; if p95 latency spikes we can lower batch_size or pin to a smaller model variant and enable prefix caching. I can demo these knobs during the session.

If OpsFlow confirms EU routing and SAML we should loop in our Private/Enterprise team for packaging timelines.
